subject.title: [Bug]: Enabling Codex plugin causes Runtime to switch to OpenAI Codex and ignore configured primary model, resulting in GPT-5.4-nano TPM failures

question: Should enabling the Codex plugin ever cause existing ordinary chat sessions to run OpenAI-selected models through Codex by default, or must Codex runtime selection require an explicit user/provider/runtime choice after plugin enablement?
rationale: Current docs and code intentionally default canonical OpenAI provider routes to Codex, while the reporter’s latest evidence says plugin enablement alone can move a DeepSeek-primary setup into OpenAI Responses API execution.

options.title: Repair route drift first
options.body: Confirm and fix any stale/session-state path that promotes DeepSeek-primary chats into OpenAI/Codex, while preserving intentional OpenAI-to-Codex routing for explicit OpenAI choices.

options.title: Make Codex explicit-only
options.body: Change policy so enabling the Codex plugin never changes ordinary OpenAI chat runtime unless the user explicitly requests Codex.

options.title: Fold into resolver refactor
options.body: Treat this as acceptance coverage for the broader session model/auth state resolver before making a narrow runtime-policy change.

recommendation.title: Repair route drift first
recommendation.body: Confirm and fix any stale/session-state path that promotes DeepSeek-primary chats into OpenAI/Codex, while preserving intentional OpenAI-to-Codex routing for explicit OpenAI choices.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest recent history across OpenAI provider identity, harness policy, Codex harness, and gateway session utilities.
